q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a stainless steel kitchen sink?
title: Steel kitchen sink carbon footprint per piece
short: Weigh the stainless steel coil used per sink, including blanking scrap, and multiply by the steel supplier's per-kg figure. Add deep drawing, welding, polishing and packing energy, then divide by sinks passed.

ul: Stainless steel sheet by grade and weight.
Sound pads and coating on the underside.

p: Report per sink by bowl size and grade. Stainless steel is most of the total, so the mill's figure matters most.

example.title: Worked example: stainless steel kitchen sink unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 14,200 / 10,000 = 1.420 kg CO2 per piece

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
